claim: The CPU dense state is a contiguous array of 2^n Complex64 amplitudes in basis-index order; q0 is the least significant bit.
derivation: Index i encodes sum_q bit(q)*2^q. SIMD loads interpret each Complex64 as adjacent real and imaginary f64 values.
limitations: Applies to the dense CPU backend only.

claim: Dense amplitude storage is 16*2^n bytes: 512 MiB at 25 qubits and 16 GiB at 30 qubits.
derivation: One amplitude is two 8-byte f64 values. Multiply 16 by the number of basis states.
limitations: Amplitude payload only. Outputs, allocator overhead and scratch are excluded.

claim: A 1q gate visits disjoint amplitude pairs by inserting a zero target bit into each compressed pair index.
derivation: half=2^t; mask=half-1; i0=((k & ~mask)<<1)|(k & mask); i1=i0|half. k ranges from 0 through 2^(n-1)-1.
limitations: This is the general non-diagonal 1q matrix kernel; diagonal gates have specialized paths.

claim: The two amplitudes in a target-t pair are 16*2^t bytes apart, while each half-block is contiguous.
derivation: A block has 2^(t+1) amplitudes. Lower and upper half pointers differ by 2^t amplitudes, each 16 bytes.
limitations: Address spacing alone does not determine cache misses or latency.

claim: Each AVX2 input register packs two complex amplitudes from one half as [re0, im0, re1, im1]. Two registers supply two independent amplitude pairs.
derivation: Each _mm256_loadu_pd reads four adjacent f64 values. The lower and upper amplitude halves are loaded separately.
limitations: Lane order is ascending lane number. The 128-bit kernels pack one amplitude per register.

claim: The AVX2 complex multiply is a permute with mask 0101, a multiply by the imaginary coefficient, and an fmaddsub.
derivation: z=[x0,y0,x1,y1]; permute=[y0,x0,y1,x1]; t=ci*permute; fmaddsub(cr,z,t)=[cr*x0-ci*y0,cr*y0+ci*x0,cr*x1-ci*y1,cr*y1+ci*x1].
limitations: These are the source intrinsics. The compiled instruction stream was not captured.

claim: NEON packs one complex amplitude in [re,im], swaps lanes and fuses against a pre-negated imaginary coefficient [-ci,+ci].
derivation: vextq_f64(z,z,1) gives [im,re]; vmulq_f64(cr,z) plus vfmaq_f64(product,[-ci,+ci],swapped) gives the complex product.
limitations: NEON is the aarch64 path; it does not use 256-bit AVX lane packing.

claim: The x86 128-bit FMA path uses shuffle, multiply and fmaddsub; SSE2 uses shuffle, two multiplies, a sign XOR and add.
derivation: Both pack [re,im]. Runtime detection selects AVX2+FMA, then FMA, then the x86_64 SSE2 baseline.
limitations: The best detected tier can still fall back to a narrower full-state kernel according to target and state length.

claim: For an ordinary CPU 1q matrix on x86_64, AVX2 is selected exactly when AVX2 and FMA are available, t>=2, and either n<=13 or the parallel feature is enabled with n>=15.
derivation: Sequential full-state AVX2 requires target>=2 and slice length<=8192. With parallel at n>=15, t<=12 uses 8192-amplitude tiles, and higher targets use paired slices whose apply method selects AVX2. At n=14 the ordinary path is FMA.
limitations: Assumes valid 0<=t<n, a non-miri build, and a general dense CPU 1q gate. Excludes diagonal, controlled-pointer, MultiFused, and GPU paths. The parallel feature is a build choice, not a requested thread count.

claim: MultiFused tile application removes the full-state AVX2 length limit while retaining t>=2; single-pair pointer application uses 128-bit FMA on AVX2 hosts.
derivation: apply_tiled branches on target>=2 without the 8192-element guard. apply_pair_ptr maps both Avx2Fma and Fma to apply_pair_fma.
limitations: The target in a gathered tile is a tile coordinate and can differ from its circuit qubit index.

claim: Ordinary 1q parallel execution uses whole tiles, whole paired half-blocks, or paired subtiles according to the number and size of blocks.
derivation: B=2^(t+1), T=max(8192,B). If B<=8192 and N/T>=4 use 8192-element tiles. Else if N/T>=4 use whole B blocks split into halves. Otherwise split each pair of halves into min(8192,2^t)-element chunks.
limitations: Rayon task count need not match worker count. These branches set no thread affinity or NUMA placement.

claim: A general dense 1q gate has a conventional arithmetic count of 14*2^n FLOPs and logical amplitude traffic of 32*2^n bytes.
derivation: Each pair has four complex multiplies at 6 FLOPs and two complex adds at 2 FLOPs: 28 FLOPs. Two 16-byte reads plus two 16-byte writes give 64 bytes per pair. There are 2^(n-1) pairs, giving 0.4375 FLOP per logical byte.
limitations: FMA counts as two FLOPs. Addressing, coefficient loads, cache reuse and write allocation are excluded. The bound 32*2^n/W assumes all logical traffic crosses a memory level with sustained bandwidth W.

claim: Default cache tiles span 256 KiB through 1 MiB, derived from L2 per core and last-level cache sharing, and parallel passes can shrink tiles to expose concurrency.
derivation: The budget rounds down a clamped power of two. The L2 contribution is per physical core; the LLC contribution uses one quarter of its per-logical-CPU share. Divide bytes by 16 for amplitude count. Parallel sizing reads available hardware parallelism, not Rayon pool width.
limitations: Cache residency is assumed, not measured. PRISM_TILE_KB can override the default range to 128 KiB through 2 MiB.

claim: MultiFused can apply several gates within one tile, including gathering high-bit subcubes into contiguous scratch before processing and scattering.
derivation: The subcube route copies each selected run into tile scratch, calls apply_tiled for every gate, then copies runs back. The in-place route loops over gates inside each parallel tile. Exactly zero gathered subcubes return before gate work and stores.
limitations: The planner picks among these routes, so fused execution does not always cost one DRAM sweep per gate.

claim: CUDA stores amplitudes as interleaved f64 values interpreted as double2; resource checks budget 25 bytes per amplitude while amplitude payload remains 16 bytes.
derivation: GpuState allocates 2*2^n f64 values. The 25-byte budget adds 8 bytes of probability scratch plus 1 byte of margin. Successful device initialization clears the host amplitude vector.
limitations: The resource coefficient is not an exact allocation-size formula for every query.

claim: The ordinary CUDA 1q kernel assigns one inserted-bit amplitude pair to each thread in a 256-thread block.
derivation: k=blockIdx.x*blockDim.x+threadIdx.x. Threads with k>=2^(n-1) return. Scalar coefficient arguments describe the 2x2 matrix. This kernel directly reads and writes the global state.
limitations: Launch shape and address pattern say nothing about occupancy, achieved bandwidth or speedup.

claim: A non-diagonal CUDA MultiFused tile holds 1024 complex amplitudes in 16 KiB of shared memory and uses 512 threads with a barrier after each gate.
derivation: Ten tile qubits include the lowest five, making each warp's consecutive tile offsets contiguous global amplitudes. A pass adds at most five higher targets. Low-target gates join the first pass. Each tile is loaded once, processed across all assigned gates, then stored.
limitations: n<=10 and passes with fewer than three gates use per-gate fallback. Occupancy and throughput were not measured.

claim: With P=2^p ranks, each rank initially owns 2^(n-p) consecutive amplitudes; low physical qubit bits select local indices and high bits select rank.
derivation: L=2^(n-p), global index=rank*L+local_index. Rank count must be a power of two and the local qubit floor is checked.
limitations: After relabeling, circuit qubits map to physical positions through qubit_map rather than identity.

claim: A direct global 1q gate pairs rank r with r XOR 2^(q-local_qubits) and combines the local shard with the received shard; a global diagonal gate only scales local amplitudes.
derivation: Rank-bit zero computes m00*own+m01*remote; rank-bit one computes m11*own+m10*remote. A direct general 1q gate sends 16L bytes and receives 16L bytes per rank, tiled by exchange_chunk.
limitations: The communication volume is derived payload, excludes protocol overhead, and describes direct exchange. Default relabeling can avoid repeated direct exchanges.

claim: Default distributed relabeling moves a global target into a local bit position by exchanging a half slice and retains the new mapping for later gates.
derivation: The moving indices have local bit unequal to rank bit. Each rank sends and receives L/2 amplitudes, or 8L bytes each way. Map updates record circuit-to-physical positions. A SWAP can be map-only. Batched instruction windows can plan future victims.
limitations: Local working-set fit determines reuse. Cyclic scans can force eviction. Relabeling can be disabled or impossible when no victim remains.

claim: MPI requests MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED or higher; below MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE all MPI calls are confined to the constructing thread while Rayon workers perform memory work.
derivation: MPI receives contiguous double views of complex slices and sendrecv_pieces splits around the C int count limit. The default chunk is 2^29 complex amplitudes, or 8 GiB maximum payload per message.
limitations: The chunk size is a ceiling, not an allocation made on every call. Nothing in this source overlaps communication with compute or uses GPU-aware MPI, and multi-node scaling was not measured.

claim: Diagonal Z and Rz gates use independent complex scaling; on an AVX2+FMA host, their AVX2 route requires the parallel feature, n>=15 and target>=n-2.
derivation: The high-target branch runs when 2^n/2^(target+1)<4, equivalent to target>=n-2. It scales 4096-amplitude chunks using the AVX2 helper. Other branches call the 128-bit FMA diagonal loop. Z skips the unchanged lower member; Rz normally scales both. No cross-input products or row additions occur.
limitations: Assumes valid targets, non-miri build and AVX2+FMA availability. The aarch64 path remains 128-bit NEON. The x86 diagonal fallback without FMA is scalar. Fused matrices are checked for diagonality and do not force the general matrix kernel.
